data.source_title: ED handoffs: observed practices and communication errors
data.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods and Results; lines 241-246 of rendered PubMed record
data.source_setting: Emergency physician patient handoffs at one major metropolitan teaching hospital ED; the abstract does not identify the study hospital
data.source_period: Eight weeks of observation; calendar dates not reported in abstract
data.unit: percent of handoffs with examination omissions (447/992 patient handoffs)
data.source_evidence_basis: Two investigators observed handoffs. Authors defined an error/omission by comparing clinically significant examination or laboratory findings in physician documentation with what was reported differently or omitted in verbal handoff. Examination omissions: 447 (45.1%); examination errors: 130 (13.1%). Fewer examination omissions were associated with use of written/electronic support.
data.limitations: Single center, observational, older study; denominator here is patient handoffs, not 110 sessions. Findings are against documentation and do not establish patient harm, causation, or rates at other hospitals. Abstract does not state observation dates.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Optional synthetic handoff variation: a documented examination finding is absent from verbal sign-out; learner may notice and clarify it. Do not use the study percentage as a scenario probability or local benchmark.
